subject: Conversation emit delay — interim bridge configs and follow-up
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike@starlight.ai>, Support Team <support@starlight.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conversation emit delay — initial update and short-term mitigations

Hi Mike / Starlight team,

Thanks for the report this morning. We observed elevated tail latency affecting streaming endpoints between ~08:40–09:05 PT for the region your org is routed through. Symptoms you reported (sporadic pauses in the token stream and occasional multi-second gaps) match our telemetry.

What we know so far:
- Root symptom: increased token emission delay tied to a burst of concurrent long-history sessions on a subset of edge shards.
- Scope: ~3% of your streaming requests during the window; 98th-percentile emission delay rose to ~3.2s.
- Impact: visible stuttering in real-time chat flows and some reconnections. No request loss or content corruption.

Immediate actions we’ve applied (short-term):
- Temporary per-customer rate shaping on your route to smooth bursts.
- Increased max-concurrent-requests on hot shards for 30 minutes while we evict a bad kernel placement.
- Enabled conservative prefix caching for chat sessions originating from Starlight to reduce KV lookups.

Recommended short-term mitigations on your side to minimize user-visible impact:
1) If you can, set client-side chunking timeout to 4s and retry-on-gap with jitter (recommended backoff: 200–600ms).
2) Temporarily reduce your long-history tail retention for interactive sessions (remove >7k token context for the heaviest routes).
3) If you rely on our streaming SSE, allow a 2s grace window before triggering client reconnects.

Attachments: we included a short snapshot of logs and an interim bridge config we propose applying to your routing entry.

We’re continuing triage and will follow up with a detailed post-incident summary and permanent remediation timeline. If you want an immediate call to walk through the temporary configs, I’m available at 10:00 PT.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
Attachment stubs: starlight_incident_snapshot-logs.txt (text), interim-bridge-configs.yaml (text)

From: Mike Chen <mike@starlight.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Support Team <support@starlight.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conversation emit delay — initial update and short-term mitigations

Kim, thanks for the fast update — appreciate the clear notes. A few quick items from our side:

- We saw the stalls in the web client and in our mobile SDK at roughly the same times. Users reported a spinner freeze of ~2–4s before the stream resumed.
- We can apply the client-side chunking timeout and grace window suggestions today; pushing a mobile SDK patch will take a couple of hours.
- We’d like Redwood to apply the interim bridge config you mentioned while we push the client fix. Can you confirm what the expected behavior will be for sessions with >10k tokens?

Also, if there’s a short (15–20m) sync with your ops lead and our infra person, we’d like to join. Proposed participants: Ben Carter (Redwood ops), Logan Wright (Redwood support), our infra lead Jason Park.

-Mike
VP Product — Starlight AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Conversation emit delay — ops action and config apply (internal)

Forwarding customer ask and adding ops notes.

Action items for ops/infra:
- I’m applying the interim-bridge-configs.yaml to Starlight’s routing entry in us-west-2 now (will push during low-risk window at 10:10 PT).
- Evan will monitor shard hotness and token queue depth for the next 60 minutes after the change.
- If emission delay does not improve within 10 minutes, escalate to kernel placement rollback (rolling to previous kernel build).

Notes on expected behavior for heavy contexts (>10k tokens):
- Interim config trims active prefix cache retention for sessions over 8k tokens; clients will receive shorter initial prefixes which reduces KV pressure.
- We’ll also enable a conservative streaming chunk size (4–8 tokens) to stabilize emit cadence; that can increase token counts slightly but reduces pauses.

I’ll join the sync with Starlight, Ben

—Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike@starlight.ai>, Support Team <support@starlight.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conversation emit delay — interim bridge configs and follow-up

Hi Mike — quick status and next steps after the config change: 

- What we changed: interim-bridge-configs.yaml rolled at 10:12 PT. We trimmed prefix retention for >8k contexts and set conservative chunking on your route.
- Immediate result: your 98th-percentile emit delay reduced from ~3.2s to ~600–800ms within 7 minutes post-deploy. Client-visible stutter frequency dropped to <0.5% of requests in the monitored window.
- Next steps for Redwood: full kernel-placement audit and a permanent fix scheduled for next week (target: 2026-12-22). We’ll share the postmortem doc and a timeline for a non-disruptive kernel rollout.

Customer-facing recommendations (recap):
1) Deploy client-side chunking timeout (4s) and graceful retry with jitter.
2) If possible, temporarily truncate very long histories (>10k tokens) for interactive routes while we complete the kernel remediation.
3) Use the provided interim-bridge-configs.yaml as-is; we’ll revert it once the permanent fix is validated.

We’ll also apply a goodwill credit for the affected window; Evelyn will follow up with a formal credit memo and the postmortem link.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll send the full incident summary and the postmortem link once the audit completes.

Best,
Kim
